# Wisdom of Solomon Chapter 5 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Wisdom 5 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/WIS_005_page_001.jpg

---

5:1 Then the righteous man will stand with great boldness in the presence of those who have afflicted him and made light of his labors.

5:2 When they see him, they will be shaken with terrible fear, and they will be amazed at the unexpectedness of his salvation.

5:3 They will speak among themselves in repentance, and in anguish of spirit they will groan, and say:

5:4 "This was the man whom we once held in derision, and as a byword of reproach — we fools! We thought his life was madness and his death without honor.

5:5 How has he been counted among the sons of God? And how is his lot among the holy ones?

5:6 So we strayed from the way of truth, and the light of righteousness did not shine for us, and the sun did not rise upon us.

5:7 We were worn out on the path of lawlessness and destruction, and we traveled through trackless wastes; but the way of the Lord we have not known.

5:8 What did our arrogance profit us? And what has our boasted wealth brought us?

5:9 All those things have passed away like a shadow, and like a message running ahead,

5:10 like a ship that passes through the billowing water, of which, when it has gone by, there is no trace to be found, nor a path of its keel in the waves;

5:11 or as when a bird flies through the air, no evidence of its passage is found, but the light wind, lashed by the stroke of its pinions and divided by the violent rush of the moving wings, is passed through, and afterward no sign of its coming is found there;

5:12 or as when an arrow is shot at a target, the air thus struck is divided at once and reunites, so that its passage is not perceived.

5:13 So we also, as soon as we were born, ceased to be, and had no sign of virtue to show, but were consumed in our wickedness."

5:14 For the hope of the ungodly is like thistledown carried on the wind, and like thin foam driven before a storm; and like smoke it is scattered by the wind, and it passes as the memory of a guest who stayed but one day.

5:15 But the righteous live forever, and their reward is with the Lord; the Most High takes care of them.

5:16 Therefore they will receive a glorious crown and a beautiful diadem from the hand of the Lord; for with his right hand he will cover them, and with his arm he will shield them.

5:17 He will take his zeal as his whole armor, and will arm all creation to repel his enemies;

5:18 he will put on righteousness as a breastplate, and will wear impartial justice as a helmet;

5:19 he will take holiness as an invincible shield,

5:20 and will sharpen stern wrath as a sword; and creation will join him to fight against the senseless.

5:21 Shafts of lightning will fly with true aim, and will leap from the clouds to the target, as from a well-drawn bow,

5:22 and hailstones full of wrath will be hurled as from a catapult; the water of the sea will rage against them, and rivers will ruthlessly overwhelm them;

5:23 a mighty wind will rise against them, and like a tempest it will winnow them away. Lawlessness will lay waste the whole earth, and evil-doing will overturn the thrones of kings.

---

*EMET notes: The chapter begins with the dramatic reversal scene — the wicked see the righteous vindicated. Their speech of regret (vv. 3–13) parallels and reverses the earlier speech of the ungodly (ch. 2). Verse 14: "thistledown" (achuron) — chaff/dust of grain. Verses 17–23 deploy the full panoply of divine warfare: God arms himself with righteousness (breastplate), justice (helmet), holiness (shield), wrath (sword) — later echoed in Eph 6:13–17.*
